paragraphs: David wanted to show kindness to Hanun because Hanun's father had shown kindness to him (1 Chronicles 19:2). But the Ammonite princes asked Hanun, "Just because David has sent you comforters, do you really believe he is showing respect for your father?" (1 Chronicles 19:3). Friend, one suspicious voice in your ear can turn a kind gesture into a crime scene. Hanun believed that theory over the kindness standing right in front of him, and it ended in war.

Joab shows a better way to handle pressure. With enemies in front of him and behind him, he tells his brother Abishai that if one side is too strong, "then you will come to my rescue" (1 Chronicles 19:12). Then he finishes with "May the LORD do what is good in His sight." (1 Chronicles 19:13). Friend, I can't carry one cookie box without yelling for backup, so I say do your part, ask for help, and leave the result with the LORD.

So here's the big idea, baker. Ask before you assume the worst about someone's kindness, because a bad guess can cost you more than a thousand talents of silver (1 Chronicles 19:6). And when the battle in front of you is big, be strong, stand with your people, and trust the LORD to do what is good in His sight.
